name: Homemade Neapolitan pizza with preferment (3-day protocol)
description: Neapolitan pizza recipe with Caputo Pizzeria 00 flour, a preferment, 64% hydration and long cold fermentation, with a 3-day schedule and oven guide.
keywords: neapolitan pizza, neapolitan pizza recipe, neapolitan pizza dough, pizza napoletana, preferment, poolish, homemade pizza, Caputo Pizzeria
recipeIngredient: 325 g crushed peeled tomatoes with salt
Extra virgin olive oil to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Make the preferment
recipeInstructions.text: Dry-mix 400 g of flour with 0.8 g of yeast. Add 400 g of water and stir into a rough paste with no dry flour left. Cover. Leave 1 h at room temperature. Refrigerate (7 °C) for about 20 h.

recipeInstructions.name: Initial mix
recipeInstructions.text: Use the preferment straight from the fridge, without a long warm-up. Dissolve 23 g of salt in 94 g of water. Add 400 g of flour and the salted water to the preferment. Mix until all the flour is hydrated. It doesn't need to be smooth. Cover and rest. Time develops the gluten for you.

recipeInstructions.name: Bassinage
recipeInstructions.text: Add the remaining 18 g of water in small portions. Only add more once the dough has absorbed the previous one. If the dough gets sticky, don't add flour.

recipeInstructions.name: Develop the gluten
recipeInstructions.text: Alternate rests and sets of folds, without aggressive kneading. Stop when the dough is smooth, rounded, elastic and has surface tension.

recipeInstructions.name: Oil last
recipeInstructions.text: With the dough already structured, add 12 g of olive oil a little at a time. Work it in with pincers and folds until fully absorbed.

recipeInstructions.name: Post-oil rest and lamination
recipeInstructions.text: Rest 3–5 min. Lamination: gently stretch the dough into a rectangle on the bench and fold it over itself. No rolling pin, no tearing. Shape into a ball. Rest 15 min. Do gentle folds and rest for about 1 h.

recipeInstructions.name: Divide and ball
recipeInstructions.text: Divide into 5 dough balls of 270 g (total dough 1,348 g). Ball with surface tension and seal the base well. Covered container, in the fridge for about 24 h.

recipeInstructions.name: Temper the dough balls
recipeInstructions.text: Take them out of the fridge about 4 h before baking (reference: ~26 °C). Ready when: risen, lots of small bubbles and a few bigger ones, airy sides, holds its shape, no collapse, relaxed. In a 1 L tub, the reference is the dough reaching halfway.

recipeInstructions.name: Prepare sauce and cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Crush 1 can(s) of peeled tomatoes by hand (no blender, no cooking). Season with 4–5 g of salt per can. No sugar. Cut 350 g of mozzarella into small pieces and let it drain.

recipeInstructions.name: Preheat the BIG HORN
recipeInstructions.text: Top element at 450 °C, bottom element at 380 °C. If you have an infrared thermometer, measure the centre of the stone and note it down.

recipeInstructions.name: Stretch the dough
recipeInstructions.text: One dough ball at a time. Dip it lightly in flour. Press from the centre outwards with your fingertips, pushing the gas towards the rim. Leave a 1–1.5 cm rim unpressed. On the first bake, 2 cm made the cornicione too thick. Finish by hand to ~30–32 cm. No rolling pin.

recipeInstructions.name: Top and launch
recipeInstructions.text: 65 g of sauce, 70 g of mozzarella spaced out, basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Leave patches of tomato showing. Before launching, give it a small sideways shake: the whole pizza must slide. Prosciutto and rocket go on after the oven.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake and turn
recipeInstructions.text: At 25–30 s, check whether it has enough structure to turn 180°. Then make small turns until the colour is even. The first pizza calibrates the oven. Use the diagnosis below. Let the stone recover before the next pizza.
